text:
lisa: Quick FYI — Product is planning a promo that moves a chunk of Starter customers into Pro (starts next Thu). They expect a ~35% conversion of active starters and a 20-30% TOken throughput uplift for the first 10 days. Can infra run a short forecast for GPU hours, regional capacity constraints, and an estimated cost delta? Need recommendation on pre-warming Dedicated pools vs relying on smart routing. cc @raj @marta

raj: Do we have the exact pricing/quotas change? Is this increasing per-token price or just removing a cap that pushes clients to Pro? Need assumed qps and avg seq len to run sims. Also: any hard rate-limit changes we should account for?

lisa: It's a plan to remove the Starter per-minute throughput bucket for certain customers and bundle them into Pro with higher per-minute quotas but same per-token price. Product gave us: expected +35% active conversions, mean qps per converted user +15%, avg seq len from 120 -> 160 for the new workflows. They flagged EU and US as primary regions. No explicit rate-limit increases, but quotas per-account will be higher which will increase parallel requests.

marta: Ran a quick back-of-envelope using current baseline: baseline = 600k GPU hours/month (served across us-west/us-east/eu-west). Model assumptions: 35% more Pro users, 15% qps uplift, sequence length +33% => token-hours uplift ~= 30%. So delta ~= +180k GPU hours/month. For short-term 10-day promo spike we're looking at ~+60k GPU hours. Rough cost impact @ our internal marginal of $0.80/GPU-hour => extra $144k/mo and $48k for the 10-day spike (ballpark).

marta: Capacity-wise if we keep current packing/batching: need extra steady-state capacity of ~10 A100s in us-west, ~6 in eu-west, ~8 in us-east to hit 99th pct SLOs. For the 10-day spike add ~3-4 extra nodes in each region as buffer. These numbers assume we can keep auto-batching params the same; if we tweak batching to favor lower latency cost increases more.

oliver: Heads-up on region constraints: eu-west has limited p4 inventory next week (we're at 85% reserved). Request to cloud is in but timelines are flaky. If we can't get extra A100s there, we should route a % of EU traffic to us-east during the 10-day window. That will increase cross-region egress cost (~$8-12k estimate) but keeps latency within SLO for most customers.

infra-bot: deploy-bot posted: "reserved-pool-update job scheduled for 2026-06-10 08:00 UTC — will not provision until approval."

raj: Mitigation options: 1) Gradual promo ramp (recommended) — a 3-day ramp to let autoscaling warm up. 2) Canary per-region 10% conversion to measure real-world seq lengths, qps. 3) Temporary soft rate-limits on non-critical routes if we see queue blowups. Product should be OK with gradual ramp.

marta: Proposed runbook (short):
- Day -3: Approve & open reservation requests in us-west/us-east/eu-west.
- Day -2: Spin up pre-warm dedicated nodes: 10 A100 (us-west), 8 A100 (us-east), 6 A100 (eu-west).
- Day -1: Run canary with 5% of conversions in each region, monitor these queries: 
  - prometheus: sum(rate(tokens_generated_total[5m])) by (region)
  - latency p95/p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,region))
  - queue depth: sum(gpu_request_queue_length) by (region)
- Promo day 0-2: Ramp conversions 10% -> 33% -> 100% over 3 days (automated via product toggle).
- During spike: If p99 latency > target OR queue_depth growth > 20%: trigger routing policy to fall back to compatible quantized model (q4) for non-critical customers and start cross-region spill to us-east for EU.
- Cost control: enable autoscale cool-down tweaks and temporarily cap burst spot usage to avoid surprise spend.
- Post-mortem: Evaluate actual GPU-hour delta and adjust reserved commitments.

marta: Quick commands for infra to run pre-checks:
```
# check reserved capacity
cloudctl reservations list --region eu-west --filter status=active
# estimate current hourly GPU usage
promql 'sum(rate(gpu_active_hours_total[1h])) by (region)'
```

raj: Sounds good. One ask: can we publish expected SLA impact matrix to product so they can communicate to customers? e.g., if we route EU->US, add note about ~30-70ms added latency for affected customers.

lisa: Yes please do. Product wants the customer-facing note and cost delta numbers by EOD tomorrow. Marta/raj — can you finalize numbers and suggested promo ramp schedule? Also add a fallback decision tree for on-call if things go south.

oliver: I can follow up on cloud quotas and try to escalate for eu-west capacity. If we don't get adds, we'll prepare routing rules and test egress paths today.

marta: Will do. I'll post final numbers and the condensed runbook by 16:00 UTC tomorrow.

raj: I'll draft the SLA impact blurb and the emergency on-call playbook.

lisa: Awesome, thanks all :thumbsup:
